We are supposed to care for each other, especially family... You say it is hard because no one is probably helping you and sharing responsibilities

We are all humans, we can all get sick, we are expected to all turn old, we don't want to be a burden to anyone, but we all do deserve the love and care from our loved ones

snippet.textDisplay:
High stress can also cause anxiety to the nth degree. And high cortisol levels... making you feel like you are in a constant state of flight or fight ... I have had this while being the caregiver to my mother before she died and even after because I had to handle her affairs after she passed. I have never felt more alone, stressed, anxiety-ridden, unable to sleep, waking up in a panic... It gave me painful gastritis. It took me a good year to get myself right mentally and physically. Take care of yourselves!!!

Thank you, Mel, for talking about this

snippet.textDisplay: @lil_brabrathankyou. I appreciate your comment, and empathy. Really!  11 months on from my comment, I am in a better mindset. Therapy has helped. snippet.textDisplay:
Being a caregiver to my aging mother has been the worst thing for both of us. Neither of us wanted to be in this position. But we don’t have anyone else who can take over full time.

Insurance doesn’t even confer for respite care. I have never felt more numb and depressed at the same time. To the point I’ve told her I might need some professional help. But I can’t even do that because who’s going to take care of her while I’m at the hospital? No one. NO ONE around me wants this responsibility placed on my shoulders.

I have no siblings to help. Everyone else has to their own lives to deal with. I honestly don’t want to be her caregiver anymore because the resentment is so hard to fight. I feel like my life isn’t my own. I’m just her nurse and driver

snippet.textDisplay:
Saya merawat ibu mertua saya yang mengidap kanker usus yang sudah menyebar. Sudah dua tahun saya dan suami merawatnya. Saya tidak hanya mengurus kebutuhannya, tapi juga berdagang untuk menghidupi kami bertiga, saya juga yang bertanggungjawab atas kebersihan rumah kami.
Akhir-akhir ini saya merasa takut pada diri saya. Saya menjadi mudah marah untuk hal-hal kecil. Dan saya sering membayangkan hal-hal buruk yang bisa saya lakukan pada mertua saya agar saya lepas dari semua tekanan ini. Setiap kali saya berada di sekitar mertua saya, dia selalu menyakiti saya dengan kata-katanya, tuntutannya, dan caranya menatap saya seolah saya tidak berguna karena saya dan suami belum memiliki keturunan.
Saya ingin berteriak di depan mukanya, tapi saya menahan diri karena dia adalah ibu dari suami saya.
Perasaan ini benar-benar mengerikan. Bahkan, saya tidak dapat lagi mengenali diri saya sendiri.

snippet.textDisplay: Thank you Mel - this is so true. I gave up work to become a f/t dad 19 years ago. There were a number of factors for this decision. A couple of years in I was diagnosed with multiple chronic illnesses. I’ve kept on going, supporting my wife’s career and getting the boys through school. But I’m so burnt out now - not helped by the complex trauma re-emerging of an incredibly dysfunctional childhood. My days and weeks are measured out by the meds that keep me alive. I’m 50 and have no personal financial security or job prospects. I feel life is over and just feel lost and forgotten. But thank you for giving voice for something that seems to go largely ignored when one person takes on the primary caregiving and home making roles.

snippet.textDisplay: I joined a few support groups on Facebook thinking it was a safe space to vent and share my frustration.....and then, apparently a "friend" that knows my sister decided to share my less than complimentary coments with my sister and she called me out. The relationship with my sister's is forever changed and over.   Thank you for free space to vent.

snippet.textDisplay:
Mel.. You're right again! I think I'm filling up my plate too much sometimes. I'm becoming a recovery specialist, building a new peer support group in my neighborhood, trying to find a new job, and getting ready to send the kids back to school soon. I'm overwhelmed! But the best advice I've ever gotten was to Schedule your time OFF! Put it in your calendar that you're doing NOTHING this day.. and stick to doing Nothing. Nothing is something to people who need "me-time"
I also started using the insight timer meditation app and the down dog yoga app.. it's heavenly!!
